alert.text: 3 of 10 years (2016–2025) had 5 or more days in a row with almost no rain in July and August (NASA POWER). That is why, when comparing, how well each crop copes with a lack of water counts more.

criteria.reason: It is the same crop: it does not diversify.

Sorghum copes better with a lack of water: the Ky factor is 0.9 (FAO; below 1 = tolerant). In this area, 3 of 10 years (2016–2025) had 5 or more days in a row with almost no rain in July and August (NASA POWER). Total rain is enough (1272 mm on average from May to October; CENTA gives 550 mm for the cycle): the risk is in the dry spells.
Growing sorghum again is not a rotation: you lose what changing crops gives, such as breaking its pests and diseases (FAO).

scenarios.summary: Sow maize after sorghum. The crop changes, but sorghum and maize belong to the same family (grasses).
scenarios.limitation: Maize loses more yield when water is short: the Ky factor is 1.25 (FAO; above 1 = sensitive).

criteria.reason: The crop changes, but sorghum and maize belong to the same family (grasses).

Maize loses more yield when water is short: the Ky factor is 1.25 (FAO; above 1 = sensitive). In this area, 3 of 10 years (2016–2025) had 5 or more days in a row with almost no rain in July and August (NASA POWER). Total rain is enough (1272 mm on average from May to October; CENTA gives 500 to 700 mm for the cycle): the risk is in the dry spells.
The crop changes, but sorghum and maize are both cereals: no legume comes in, and legumes are the ones that fix nitrogen.

scenarios.summary: Sow beans after sorghum. The crop changes and so does the family (a cereal and a legume).
scenarios.limitation: Beans lose more yield when water is short: the Ky factor is 1.15 (FAO; above 1 = sensitive).

criteria.reason: The crop changes and so does the family (a cereal and a legume).

Beans lose more yield when water is short: the Ky factor is 1.15 (FAO; above 1 = sensitive). In this area, 3 of 10 years (2016–2025) had 5 or more days in a row with almost no rain in July and August (NASA POWER). Total rain is enough (1272 mm on average from May to October; CENTA gives 228 mm for the cycle): the risk is in the dry spells.
Beans are a legume and fix nitrogen (CENTA). Sowing them after sorghum is a rotation, which also breaks pests and diseases (FAO).

sources.name: NASA POWER Daily API
sources.note: Daily rain (PRECTOTCORR, mm/day) and maximum temperature (T2M_MAX, °C) for the approximate point of the area. It describes a cell of about 50 km, not a plot.

sources.name: FAO-56, Table 24, and FAO-66, Table 1: Ky factor
sources.note: Whole-season Ky (from FAO-33): maize 1.25, beans 1.15, sorghum 0.9. According to FAO-66, with Ky above 1 the crop is very sensitive to water deficit and with Ky below 1 it is more tolerant. These are general values, not measured in El Salvador.

sources.name: CENTA: technical guides for maize, beans and sorghum
sources.note: Maize: at least 500 to 700 mm of well distributed rain and very sensitive to waterlogging (p. 8). Beans: average use of 228 mm (p. 15), do not tolerate standing water (p. 16), fix nitrogen (p. 9) and are rotated with non-host crops against diseases (p. 30). Sorghum: 550 mm (p. 8) and very drought tolerant (p. 15). Read from archived copies of the official download links.

sources.name: MARN (El Salvador): meteorological drought and dry day
sources.note: Weak meteorological drought: 5 to 10 consecutive dry days in the rainy season; moderate: 11 to 15; strong: more than 15. Dry day: under 1 mm in 24 hours (Climatological summary for July 2023, p. 5).

sources.name: FAO: Conservation Agriculture, species diversification
sources.note: Rotation prevents crop-specific pests and diseases from carrying over to the next crop and increases nitrogen fixation. The FAO Save and Grow fact sheet on maize and legumes (2015) adds that this rotation helps maintain soil fertility.

sources.name: Your answers in the form
sources.note: Soil texture and drainage as you answered. It is not checked in the field.

sources.name: Yago method assumptions
sources.note: Illustrative team decisions, not validated locally: the area moves to a medium lack of rain if 2 in 10 years had a dry spell and to high if half or more did; sandy soil raises it one level; a Ky of 1.2 or more counts as very sensitive; repeating the crop, changing within the family and changing family score 0, 1 and 2; the top priority decides and the others break ties.
